name: elastic-line

frames.best_why: The line is stretched into a tall upward arc by the cursor, the clearest view of the elastic pull.

tagline: Thin line bends toward the cursor and springs back.
summary: A hairline drawn across a dark page that can be caught by the pointer. Moving near it drags the middle into a stretch, and letting go springs it back to a straight line.
appearance: On a black stage a single hairline runs horizontally across the full width, over dark demo copy. At rest it is perfectly straight and very thin; when pulled it bows into a smooth curve, up to a tall pointed arch, before settling flat again.
behaviour: The line draws itself in from left to right on first load. When the pointer comes within a few pixels it grabs the midpoint and stretches it toward the cursor; moving past the release threshold or leaving the area springs it back with a light wobble.
demo_content: Heading 'STASH UI', an orange asterisk, and 'Grab the line and pull. Ready-to-use animated React components...'.
search_phrases: line you can pull with mouse
use_when: A sparse editorial page wants one playful interactive detail that rewards moving the cursor across it.
avoid_when: It is a mouse-and-touch flourish with no keyboard path and needs a wide, tall area to be worth pulling.
customise: Vertical or horizontal, grab and release thresholds, stroke width and spring transitions are props; the line colour follows currentColor and the page supplies its own content.
weight_why: One SVG path updated each frame while grabbed; otherwise a spring.

a11y.note: A pointer-only flourish with no keyboard equivalent, and the spring always animates because prefers-reduced-motion is not checked.

issues: The hairline is so thin and dim that it nearly disappears at rest.
When it bows, the line crosses the paragraph and makes the text harder to read.
polish_why: Subtle, satisfying elastic interaction; the hairline is very faint at rest.
title: Elastic Line
